metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Mexican Hat, UT
metaDescription: Hold mineral rights near Mexican Hat, Utah, along the San Juan River's early oil country? We buy privately held Paradox Basin interests directly.
heroLead: Mexican Hat sits in one of the oldest oil exploration areas in the Southwest, where surface oil seeps drew wildcatters to the San Juan River decades before Aneth was ever developed.
intro: The area around Mexican Hat has a documented oil history stretching back to the early twentieth century, tied to visible surface seeps along the San Juan River that drew some of the first exploratory drilling in the region. Modern production near Mexican Hat generally connects to the same Mississippian carbonate trend that underlies the larger Aneth Field to the east, and mineral ownership here includes both privately held fee interests and land within the Navajo Nation boundary.

We buy privately held mineral and royalty interests near Mexican Hat directly. As with the surrounding area, we confirm ownership status before discussing any number, since tribal trust interests follow a separate transfer process.

sections.heading: Some of the oldest exploration history in the basin
paragraphs: The surface oil seeps near Mexican Hat were documented long before the technology existed to develop them commercially at scale, and the area's early wells, drilled in the 1900s through the 1920s, represent some of the first oil exploration in this part of Utah. That long history occasionally means older deeds and reservations in the area use unusual or outdated language, which we review carefully as part of confirming exactly what a family owns today.

sections.heading: Confirming status near the reservation boundary
paragraphs: Because Mexican Hat sits close to Navajo Nation land, we check whether a given interest is privately held fee minerals or tribal trust land as the first step, the same way we do throughout this part of San Juan County. If your interest is fee simple, we can typically proceed with a standard purchase; if it is trust land, that transfers through the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

faqs.answer: Some of the earliest documented exploration in the region, dating back to the early 1900s, tied to visible surface oil seeps along the San Juan River.

faqs.question: My family's deed uses old or unusual language. Can you still work with it?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly review older deeds and reservation language as part of confirming what a family currently owns.

faqs.question: Is my interest near Mexican Hat tribal trust land or privately owned?
faqs.answer: We confirm this first, before discussing any offer, since the two follow very different transfer processes.
